issue.title: Enhancement: [sflow] wait_for conditions rather than use sleep() for test orchestration

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the enhancement

sflow/test_sflow.py currently makes liberal use of `sleep()` calls to ensure timing coordination between the various components of the sflow path. This is very brittle; timing changes in unrelated code paths can cause these coordination pauses to become insufficient, and conversely improvements in timing would lead to lots of wasted time waiting for nothing. Further, the timing might be different depending on the device. To make this a more general test, we should identify what the actual conditions are that need to be satisfied at each stage and add explicit `wait_for()` logic in those places.

### Current Behavior

The test uses `sleep()` in the main test as well as in the PTF script to ensure that everything has been set up correctly before traffic is sent.

### Proposed Behavior

The test uses `wait_for()` with an appropriate condition instead.

resolution.title: [sflow] Replace time.sleep with wait_until for deterministic test orchestration
resolution.description:
## Description

Replace all `time.sleep()` calls in `test_sflow.py` with `wait_until()` polling on actual conditions, making tests deterministic and resilient to timing variations across platforms.

### Changes

| Sleep | Replaced with |
|-------|--------------|
| `time.sleep(5)` after interface IP config | `wait_until` checking IP appears on interface |
| `time.sleep(2)` after `config sflow enable/disable` | `wait_until` checking `show sflow` admin state |
| `time.sleep(2)` after feature enable | `wait_until` checking feature status |
| `time.sleep(2-10)` before PTF traffic tests | `wait_until` checking SAI samplepacket config in Redis |
| `time.sleep(2)` after collector add/del | `wait_until` checking collector config reflected |

All 14 `time.sleep()` calls removed. The `time` import is no longer needed.

Fixes #21168
